events.subject: Welcome to nights
body: Your first week. Three things: write everything down, never search anyone, and call me if you are not sure.
The Field Manual in your notebook grows with every case. Read it.

events.subject: Marisol
events.body: Marisol told me how you handled 1412. Thank you for treating her fairly. I have already reminded the whole team about doors on trolleys.

events.subject: Your reports
events.body: Your 1412 report runs to two pages for a laptop that was never stolen. Night officers patrol; they do not write novels. Cut it down.

choices.label: Reply that every finding is referenced, and copy Desmond Okafor
choices.outcome: Desmond backs you in one line: "Keep writing them like that." Colm does not reply.

choices.label: Promise to keep future reports shorter
choices.outcome: Colm is pleased. Your next report leaves out the custody references, and Desmond sends it back.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.outcome: Colm takes the silence as agreement and complains about you at the supervisors' meeting.

events.subject: Last night at the Lobby Bar
body: The gentleman from your bar is awake and talking. The AED was on him and shocking before we were through the door, and your staff had the lift held. That is what saves people.
Whoever trained your bar team on the AED: keep doing it.

events.subject: Claim TM-55102
events.body: Thank you for the preserved footage. Our counsel would like a copy before the 30th. I understand you have a release policy; what do you need from us?

choices.label: Send the footage release form and route it to Desmond Okafor for approval
choices.outcome: The request comes back signed. Desmond approves the release with counsel, and the adjuster notes how cleanly it was handled.

choices.label: Email the clip to the adjuster yourself
choices.outcome: Counsel hears that footage left LP without approval. Desmond asks you to his office.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.outcome: The adjuster chases twice, then writes to the General Manager.

events.subject: Supervisor
body: You run the night shift now. Ines and the Tessmore guards report to you, and you will be audited on keys and doors, not only on cases.
Two habits: read the alarm log every week, and never let anyone fear telling you they lost a key.

events.subject: Thank you
events.body: Lucia got us the soft wrist coils. Everyone on my floor wears them now. Thank you for telling them it was not my fault.

events.subject: Bread deliveries
events.body: Chef tells me deliveries now need an LP officer at the dock. It is slowing the morning. Can we go back to the old way until the intercom is in?

choices.label: Explain the theft and keep the door shut; offer a fixed delivery window with an officer standing by
choices.outcome: Rafael grumbles, then agrees once he sees the clip. The bakery moves to 05:00.

choices.label: Agree to let the clerk prop it for ten minutes
choices.outcome: The door is propped again within a week. The alarm log fills up.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.outcome: Rafael takes it to the General Manager as LP being unhelpful.

events.subject: My case
events.body: The police found my case at the ferry terminal, without the laptop but with my mother's watch. Thank you for getting them there so fast, and for being honest with me that morning.
events.headline: Harbourfront thief stopped at the ferry terminal

events.subject: E-77
body: The vendor confirms E-77 is a genuine portable encoder from a batch sold to another hotel group two years ago and reported stolen. DS Calloway is interested.
Thirty-one keys in nineteen nights, and a man in a grey cap who knew where the trolleys stand. Somebody is shopping in our building. Keep your notebook close.

events.subject: Floor 14, the other night
body: The call came in fast and you met us at the panel with plans and keys. Holding the warm door shut was the right call: the room was well alight behind it.
We'd like to walk the building with you for a pre-incident plan. Thursdays suit the watch.

events.subject: Impairment notices
events.body: Our property engineers were pleased with the floor 14 impairment notice and the drain test result. Could you send us the hotel's impairment procedure, so we can agree it applies to every floor?

choices.label: Send the procedure and the last fire watch log, through Desmond Okafor
choices.outcome: Tarrowby's engineers accept the procedure as written and note it on the hotel's risk file.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.outcome: The request is repeated at the renewal meeting, in front of the GM.

events.subject: Claim TM-61840 (Ashcombe)
body: Mrs Ashcombe's solicitor has written. Your photographs with the scale, the cleaning log and the L-01 clip of the rain coming in on the guests' coats answer most of their questions.
We expect to settle the medical costs quickly and without dispute. Thank you for not promising anything at the scene.

events.subject: Hot work permits
events.body: Chef says the permit process cost him a night's work on the canopy and he wants contractors to sign their own permits in future. They're professionals. Can we agree that?

choices.label: Keep LP-issued permits, and offer to pre-approve planned jobs the day before
choices.outcome: Rafael accepts once he hears about the duct wrap. Planned jobs now get their permit at 17:00 the day before.

choices.label: Let contractors sign their own permits
choices.outcome: Within a month a contractor grinds in the dish area with the detectors still live and no fire watch. Two engines attend.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.outcome: Rafael takes it to the GM as LP being difficult.

events.subject: Two weeks on
body: The outcome has been decided and both parties told. I checked in with Keziah and Sunniva as you suggested; both are still on section B and say the briefings have changed.
Thank you for keeping the findings to the evidence. It made my decision easier to defend.

events.subject: The 2,208
events.body: Do I write off the banquet store gap in September's accounts, or is there anything we can recover?

choices.label: Notify Tarrowby under the employee dishonesty cover for the proven night, with the evidence pack; write off the rest
choices.outcome: Tarrowby accepts the proven loss less the excess. The rest is written off with the new controls noted.

choices.label: Claim the whole 2,208 as theft
choices.outcome: Tarrowby asks for evidence for the other two events and there is none. The claim is cut back and the adjuster notes it.

choices.label: Leave it to finance
choices.outcome: Hamish writes it all off.

events.subject: Re-audit
events.body: Re-audit complete: 96.2%, no critical items failed. The laundry staging bay works and the B1 route was clear on both of my unannounced visits. A good corrective action plan, properly closed out.

events.subject: E-77, again
body: The encoder batch E-77 came from was sold through a lock-hardware reseller that has since closed. One of its other customers is your own company's airport hotel, the Veldane Airport Port Avener, which has had eleven rooms entered with valid keys this year.
Same shared-login trick, same timing. Whoever this is knows Veldane systems from the inside. Can you find out who had that login before it was taped under a keyboard?

events.subject: My night lads
events.body: I hear you're taking nights in-house. Two of my officers are the best you've had. Will you see them right?

choices.label: Tell him they are welcome to apply and will be assessed like everyone else
choices.outcome: Both apply. One is hired on merit; Callum thanks you for being straight with him.

choices.label: Promise both of them jobs
choices.outcome: HR has to explain to twelve other applicants why two posts were never open. Priyanka is not pleased.

choices.label: Leave it
choices.outcome: The officers hear nothing and assume the worst. One leaves Tessmore early, and nights are short-handed for a week.

A theft claim on another floor goes badly. The investigation repeats a habit from "{mission}" ({choice}) and the guest's lawyer asks for the file.
Someone talks their way into a room that is not theirs, the way the gap in "{mission}" allowed ({choice}).
A guest dispute escalates on the floor. Staff repeat the approach from "{mission}" ({choice}) and a complaint reaches the brand.
A guest collapses in the spa. Staff repeat the approach from "{mission}" ({choice}) and the response is minutes slower than it should be.
Another unattended bag turns up at the ballroom. The team handles it the way "{mission}" went ({choice}) and the evening is disrupted for nothing, or not taken seriously enough.
Footage a claimant needed is gone or cannot be verified, the way "{mission}" went ({choice}). The insurer pays out and asks questions.
A key control gap from "{mission}" ({choice}) is still open when someone tries the same door again.
A back door is found propped again, the habit left from "{mission}" ({choice}). Stock goes missing from receiving.
The bell stand releases another bag on a name and a number, the gap from "{mission}" ({choice}). The guest's lawyer writes to the GM.
The fire authority reviews the night of "{mission}" ({choice}) and writes to the GM asking for the hotel's fire procedures and training records.
The claimant's solicitor quotes the scene from "{mission}" ({choice}). The insurer reserves its position and the excess goes up.
The handling of "{mission}" ({choice}) reaches an employment tribunal claim. The hotel's process is criticised in the hearing.
After "{mission}" ({choice}), the banquet store keeps losing stock. Finance flags LP in the month-end pack.
The re-audit finds the same gap as "{mission}" ({choice}). The regional office puts the hotel on its watch list.
The staffing decision in "{mission}" ({choice}) shows: nights are thin when an incident needs two people.
